correctness.rationale: Reexpanded the successive noisy Picard iterates to D=(1-rho)^2 s-(2-rho)e0+e1, W=((1-rho)s-e0)^2 and Z=s-W/D. The support minimum Dmin=d-(3-rho)eta gives the sharp eta_c. Below it the transform is continuous on the compact error square. At equality D vanishes at precisely one corner and W has positive limit; two-dimensional triangle scaling gives tail K t^-2 (K=2s^2/[(2-rho)(3-rho)^2]); for eta>eta_c the pole cuts a positive-length line, giving T_eta t^-1 via conditional widths. Tail integration proves exact p-moment thresholds p<2 at equality and p<1 above. Exact reciprocal-square quadrant integral gives precritical EZ^2=2K log(eta_c/(eta_c-eta))+O(1). Independently verified rational rho=1/2,s=1: eta_c=1/10, K=16/75, 2K=32/75 and T_(1/5)=403/1296; these checks corroborate, not replace, the asymptotic proof.

These facts are meaningful for deciding whether clipping/regularization is needed, without claiming generic noisy Anderson convergence.
